arxiv-2302-13362.title: The Doctrine of Cyber Effect: An Ethics Framework for Defensive Cyber Deception
arxiv-2302-13362.creator: Quanyan Zhu
arxiv-2302-13362.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Quanyan Zhu. The lack of established rules and regulations in cyberspace is attributed to the absence of agreed-upon ethical principles, making it difficult to establish accountability, regulations, and laws. Addressing this challenge requires examining cyberspace from fundamental philosophical principles. This work focuses on the ethics of using defensive deception in cyberspace, proposing a doctrine of cyber effect that incorporates five ethical principles: goodwill, deontology, no-harm, transparency, and fairness.

arxiv-2306-05633.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Maximilian Zinkus, Yinzhi Cao, Matthew D. Green. Protecting the confidentiality of private data and using it for useful collaboration have long been at odds. Modern cryptography is bridging this gap through rapid growth in secure protocols such as multi-party computation, fully-homomorphic encryption, and zero-knowledge proofs. However, even with provable indistinguishability or zero-knowledgeness, confidentiality loss from leakage inherent to the functionality may partially or even completely compromise secret values without ever falsifying proofs of security.

arxiv-2402-05106.creator: Rafael Silva de Alencar, William Alberto Cruz Castañeda, Marcellus Amadeus
arxiv-2402-05106.description: Abstract This work presents the early development of a model of image captioning for the Brazilian Portuguese language. We used the GRIT (Grid - and Region-based Image captioning Transformer) model to accomplish this work. GRIT is a Transformer-only neural architecture that effectively utilizes two visual features to generate better captions.

pmc-11359916.title: Development of a Neural Network for Target Gas Detection in Interdigitated Electrode Sensor-Based E-Nose Systems
pmc-11359916.creator: Kadir Kaya, Mehmet Ali Ebeoğlu, Marijo Buzuk, Maša Buljac, Nives Vladislavić
pmc-11359916.description: In this study, a neural network was developed for the detection of acetone, ethanol, chloroform, and air pollutant NO2 gases using an Interdigitated Electrode (IDE) sensor-based e-nose system. A bioimpedance spectroscopy (BIS)-based interface circuit was used to measure sensor responses in the e-nose system. The sensor was fed with a sinusoidal voltage at 10 MHz frequency and 0.707 V amplitude.

pmc-11520749.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundThere is a need to better understand ulcerative colitis (UC) patient and healthcare provider (HCP) treatment satisfaction, acceptability, and preferences.MethodsTwo international, cross-sectional, web-based surveys were conducted among participants of a phase 3 mirikizumab study (NCT03519945). The questions captured moderate-to-severe UC patients’ experience, HCPs’ perception of patients’ experience, and HCPs’ own experience with mirikizumab administration through intravenous (IV) infusions and subcutaneous (SC) injections.ResultsRespondents included 93 patients and 42 HCPs from 11 countries.

pmc-13135309.description: BACKGROUND:Bronchoscopic lung volume reduction (BLVR) offers several advantages over lung volume reduction surgery, such as faster recovery, fewer complications, and reduced infection risk; however, it also carries a risk of pneumothorax (PTX). uslaw-usc-t46-s10907.title: 46 U.S.C. § 10907 — Permission to make complaint
uslaw-usc-t46-s10907.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t46-s10907.description: United States Code, Title 46 (Shipping); Part G (Merchant Seamen Protection And Relief); Chapter 109 (Proceedings On Unseaworthiness). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) A master may not refuse to permit, deny the opportunity to, or hinder a seaman who wishes to make a complaint authorized by this chapter. (b) A master violating this section is liable to the United States Government.
